test_case: Mobile/test/service_widgets_test.dart: ConfirmationSheet a Booked status names the time once in its own line
description: Cause was not the redesign: the test used scheduledAt 2026-10-12, which is now in the past, so ServiceRequest.isOverdue made the sheet show the overdue title instead of Booked. Fixed by using 2099-10-12 in the test. App code untouched.

Resident got 404 instead of 403 on /sms/deliveries/{smsLog}/check and /recipients for a missing id (binding ran before is.admin). Fixed with prependToPriorityList(IsAdmin before SubstituteBindings) in bootstrap/app.php; applies to every admin route. New tests: resident 403 on missing id, admin still 404. New test fails without the fix.

test_case: Phase 2 gap c: service-request push accepted for zero devices
description: A status-change push to a resident with no registered device (or none that accepts it) is silent: no marker, no retry and no follow-up row. Only equipment reminders have ReminderFollowUp (reminder_not_delivered). Staff are not told the resident was not reached. No fix by decision; no test pins it.

test_case: Backend/app/Support/ReminderFollowUp.php: EquipmentAvailabilityNotifierTest the follow up is not repeated within a day
description: Same-day dedup matched new_values with LIKE '%"kind":"x"%'. MySQL's JSON column re-serialises as "kind": "x" (space after the colon), so the pattern never matched and every run wrote another reminder_not_delivered row. MariaDB 10.4 stores JSON as plain text without the space, so it passed locally. Real production bug on Railway MySQL: staff see duplicate Follow up by phone entries and the dashboard bell count is inflated. Fixed with where('new_values->kind', $kind).

test_case: Backend/app/Support/ReminderFollowUp.php: SendReturnRemindersTest the follow up is not repeated by a second run the same day
description: Same root cause and same fix as BUG-004; reached through serbis:send-return-reminders, which the Railway cron runs daily and which retries unmarked rows. Production would write a duplicate on any retry within 20 hours.

test_case: Backend/tests/Feature/ExportLogTest.php: the log row carries no record data
description: assertSame on new_values compared key order. MySQL JSON columns store object keys sorted (shortest first), MariaDB keeps insertion order. Application behaviour is correct; consumers read by key. Changed to assertEquals, which ignores associative key order.

Found 18 Oct in the production HTTP checks: none of Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy was sent, and x-powered-by: PHP/8.4.25 exposed the PHP version (php.ini-production leaves expose_php on). Fixed with App\Http\Middleware\SecurityHeaders (outermost global middleware; CSP skipped for HTML answers; HSTS only on secure requests) and expose_php=Off in the Dockerfile ini. New SecurityHeadersTest (4 tests). Not deployed.
